title: UNDP hands SESU the Ukrainian “Mines Eye” AI aerial detection system after a pilot that scanned over 360 hectares in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts
summary: Mines Eye, an aerial system whose AI detects explosive remnants of war, scanned over 360 hectares in a five-month pilot by Ukraine's emergency service; the release gives no detection counts.
account: Mines Eye is an aerial detection system that combines magnetometry with visual and infrared aerial imaging. A press release of 21 June 2025 from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Ukraine calls the system “Developed in Ukraine” but does not name the developer. The release states that “Using artificial intelligence, it detects explosive remnants of war (ERW), including anti-tank mines, even beneath vegetation”. The system produces maps and anomaly reports for operators before manual or mechanical clearance. UNDP-trained teams of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU) ran a five-month pilot. They “used the system to scan over 360 hectares of confirmed and suspected hazardous areas in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts”. The release is datelined Mykolaiv. It says that UNDP “officially handed over the Mines Eye aerial detection system to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU)”. Financial support came from the Government of Luxembourg. The handover took place at the base of SESU's Main Department in Mykolaiv oblast, with UNDP Acting Administrator Haoliang Xu present. SESU First Deputy Head Vitalii Myroniuk is quoted as saying that the technology “enables us to detect threats in areas that are too dangerous for manual inspection”. The release gives no number of items detected or confirmed, no hectares released and no accuracy figure. UNDP's release of 26 June 2025 concerned a testing exhibition with mock devices. No cited source is independent of UNDP or SESU.
purpose: Built to survey contaminated land remotely and flag explosive remnants of war, including anti-tank mines under vegetation. This lets clearance teams plan safely. The pilot was that intended use.
